title: Pipeline Forecasting & Revenue Attribution
honestyNote: This repository's own README and LEADOS-STATE.md explicitly warn that the real, committed code in that project does NOT represent a verified 139-part 'Integration Master' program, and that prior sessions found the workspace containing only a bare Next.js + Drizzle + PostgreSQL starter template with no Parts 00-107 actually implemented.

This build session started from that same bare starter template (confirmed directly: src/db/schema.ts was an empty placeholder and src/app contained only the default starter page, layout, and /api/health). There is no accessible, authoritative specification anywhere for what a 'Part 59' of this program is supposed to contain.

Rather than fabricate a fictitious history or invent requirements for an undocumented 'Part 59' and claim they came from a real spec, this session (a) built the foundational LEADOS substrate described in the project README (multi-tenant schema, deterministic scoring engine, hash-chained evidence ledger, knowledge substrate) since none of it previously existed in this workspace, and (b) added one new, coherent, fully working module on top of it — Pipeline Forecasting & Revenue Attribution — labeled 'Part 59' as requested, scoped to what a single real engineering session can deliver end-to-end with working code, not aspirational scaffolding.
No prior parts (1-58) were fabricated, no retrospective changelog entries were invented, and no claims are made about capabilities that are not present in the code below.

foundation: Multi-tenant schema (tenants, leads, decisions, knowledge_entries) in src/db/schema.ts, with a single auto-created demo tenant (src/lib/tenant.ts)

Deterministic, explainable lead-scoring engine (src/lib/scoring.ts): budget, company size, engagement, title seniority, ICP fit, and response history, each weighted and annotated with a human-readable rationale
SHA-256 hash-chained, tamper-evident evidence ledger (src/lib/ledger.ts, decisions table) with append and chain-verification functions
Knowledge substrate (knowledge_entries table) with measured / estimated / association / effect labeling
UI: / (executive overview), /leads (scoring breakdown + stage control), /decisions (ledger + chain verification), /knowledge

part59Module.name: Pipeline Forecasting & Revenue Attribution
part59Module.schema: forecasts table (src/db/schema.ts): one row per computed forecast, tied to a lead and a period, storing probability, deal value, weighted value, method, and rationale — so forecasts are a persisted, comparable history rather than an ephemeral calculation
part59Module.calcEngine: src/lib/forecast.ts — pure function computeForecast(): close probability is a transparent, documented 50/50 blend of pipeline-stage weight and the lead's deterministic score (no ML, no hidden model); won/lost stages short-circuit to 100%/0%
api: GET /api/forecasts — list forecasts joined with lead data, optional ?period filter
POST /api/forecasts — compute and persist a forecast for one lead (leadId) or all leads, writing a ledger entry per computed forecast
GET /api/forecasts/summary — aggregates the latest forecast per lead into total weighted pipeline value, value by period, and value by stage
part59Module.ui: /forecast — KPI cards (leads forecast, total deal value, weighted pipeline value), weighted value by stage, and a per-lead forecast list with plain-language rationale; 'Recompute all forecasts' triggers a fresh pass and re-logs to the evidence ledger
part59Module.ledgerIntegration: Every forecast computation appends a 'forecast.computed' entry to the same hash-chained ledger used for lead scoring and stage changes, so forecast history is auditable alongside every other decision

bugFixedDuringThisSession.issue: Initial implementation computed ledger hashes with plain JSON.stringify. PostgreSQL's jsonb column type normalizes object key order on storage, so a payload read back from the database could serialize to a different string than the exact object written, producing a false-positive 'chain broken' result on verification even though nothing was tampered with.
bugFixedDuringThisSession.fix: src/lib/ledger.ts now serializes every hashed value through a recursive, sorted-key canonical JSON form (canonicalStringify) so write-time and read-time hashes are always identical for identical content, regardless of jsonb key reordering.
bugFixedDuringThisSession.verifiedBy: Cleared and reseeded demo data, then confirmed GET /api/decisions/verify returns { ok: true } against the live preview.

whatWasBuilt.seedScript: scripts/seed.ts — creates the demo tenant, 5 demonstrative leads spanning every pipeline stage and score range, an initial forecast pass for each, and 4 knowledge entries (one per evidence category). Re-run with `npx tsx scripts/seed.ts`.

explicitlyOutOfScopeForThisPart: Parts 1-58 are not implemented, documented, or claimed as pre-existing — the foundation listed above was built this session to make Part 59 meaningful, not recovered from history
No authentication or row-level-security tenant isolation (single demo tenant only, as inherited from the README's own documented scope)
Forecast probability model is a documented linear blend, not a fitted regression, Monte Carlo simulation, or ML model
No automated test suite (vitest/playwright) was added in this session
stopCondition: This manifest marks the end of Part 59. No further parts were started.
